assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Hydrophobic
items.clue: Describes the non-polar tails, which are excluded from water

items.label: Myocardial infarction
items.clue: Death of heart muscle beyond a completely blocked vessel; a heart attack.

items.label: Coronary arteries
items.clue: Vessels branching from the aorta that supply heart muscle with oxygen and glucose.

items.label: Phospholipid bilayer
items.clue: Double sheet with heads facing water on both sides and tails forming a non-polar core

questions.stem: Which components are linked together by condensation reactions to form one phospholipid molecule?

options.text: One glycerol, two fatty acids and one phosphate group
One glycerol, three fatty acids and one phosphate group
Three glycerol molecules, one fatty acid and one phosphate group
Many fatty acid monomers joined in a chain, plus one phosphate group

questions.explanation: Glycerol has three hydroxyl groups. In a phospholipid two of them are linked by condensation to fatty acids and the third to a phosphate group, giving two hydrophobic tails and a hydrophilic head.

questions.stem: A person replaces butter with sunflower oil, keeping total fat intake the same. Why is this expected to lower their risk of cardiovascular disease?

options.text: Fat of any kind is harmful, so the benefit comes simply from eating less fat overall in the diet.
Unsaturated oils are liquid, so they cannot coat the inside of artery walls the way solid fats do.
Saturated fats are full of double bonds, which break apart in the blood and form plaques.
Swapping saturated for unsaturated fat lowers blood LDL, so less cholesterol enters artery walls.

questions.explanation: Lower LDL means less cholesterol enters damaged artery walls, so atheroma forms more slowly.

questions.stem: Phospholipids are shaken with water in a test tube, with no cells or enzymes present. What happens, and why?

options.text: Nothing organised forms, because phospholipid bilayers can only be built by enzymes inside living cells
Bilayers form, because covalent bonds link the fatty acid tails of neighbouring phospholipids
The phospholipids react with the water, because being amphipathic means acting as both an acid and a base
Bilayers form, because the hydrophilic heads face the water and the hydrophobic tails face each other

questions.explanation: The heads associate with water while the tails are excluded from it, so the molecules arrange themselves in a double layer, heads outwards and tails inwards. No enzymes are needed.

questions.stem: Lipoproteins carry cholesterol and triglycerides in blood plasma, which is mostly water. Each lipoprotein has an oily core of cholesterol and triglyceride, surrounded by a single layer of phospholipids (with some proteins). How are the phospholipids in this layer most likely arranged?

options.text: Tails facing outwards into the plasma; heads facing inwards into the oily core.
Heads facing outwards into the plasma; tails pointing inwards into the oily core.
Tails joined to one another by covalent bonds, forming a rigid shell around the core.
Mixed evenly through the oily core, as phospholipids are entirely hydrophobic like cholesterol.
